subject.title: fix(browser): prove post-action target continuity before adopting a tab

question: Should browser routes deliberately prefer a stale acted-on target that forces reselection whenever a backend cannot prove post-operation continuity, rather than preserving any inferred continuation behavior?
rationale: The patch is mechanically coherent and proof-backed, but it changes an externally observable recovery behavior for managed Playwright, extension-relay, and Chrome MCP users; only a browser owner can decide whether that fail-safe compatibility tradeoff is the supported product contract.

options.title: Approve the fail-safe contract
options.body: Accept backend-proven continuity only and merge the stale-target fallback, preventing later actions from silently moving to an unrelated tab.

options.title: Retain a compatibility path
options.body: Keep the PR open for a browser-owner-designed explicit continuation mechanism rather than restoring route-level URL or sole-tab inference.

recommendation.title: Approve the fail-safe contract
recommendation.body: Accept backend-proven continuity only and merge the stale-target fallback, preventing later actions from silently moving to an unrelated tab.

likelyOwner.reason: The canonical report defines the affected browser identity contract and the PR discussion already requests this browser-owner decision.
